[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
William Glasgow is indexed with a 10 July 1614 event at Inveresk with Musselburgh and father [[Glasgow-991|James Glasgow]]. The provider labels the event Birth; the original parish entry has not been inspected. [[Bie-55|Christina Bie]] remains the attached mother, but she is not named in this cited record.
=== Cited FamilySearch records checked, 17 October 2026 ===
The signed-in 1614 William index names father James Glasgow and a 10 July event at Inveresk with Musselburgh, but no mother. Its event label is Birth; the parish image was unavailable and remains uninspected. It does not name Christina Bie.<ref>[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4V-K87 FamilySearch, Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950, William Glasgow, 1614], provider entry inspected 17 October 2026; supplied ScotlandsPeople locator OPR 689/10/63.</ref>

The separate 1611 Catherin IGI entry reports a 6 May christening at Inveresk and names James Glasgow and Christina Bie, not Adamson. It cites batch A25031-7, film 470,979 and Patron Submissions; it is a contributed genealogy, not an inspected parish baptism. Its parent birth estimates are not independent records.<ref>[https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/2:1:M52D-TJJ FamilySearch, International Genealogical Index, Catherin Glasgow], batch A25031-7, film 470,979, provider submission inspected 17 October 2026.</ref>

No live family attachment, birth field or certainty mark has been changed. Locally, Cathrin’s exact birthday display is replaced by a conditional boundary from the reported christening; the imported birthday is retained for comparison. Christina’s maternity of William and the separate adult identities still need contemporary evidence.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-991]] is assessed at 98% (proved). The Inveresk William child record indexed 10 July 1614 names James Glasgow as father and no mother. The exact child event belongs to James’s recurring Inveresk family and expressly names the father.

Confident for this recorded son; no mother or later adult identity is supplied by the father-only index.

Next useful test: Use residence or witnesses if another Inveresk James household emerges.
